title: The Book of Haggai Decoded
author: Brittany Johnson
description: The Book of Haggai — every verse decoded into plain, modern English (DMLV).

verses.kjv: In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, saying,
verses.decoded: In the second year of King Darius, on the first day of the sixth month, the LORD spoke through the prophet Haggai to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Josedech, the high priest, saying,

verses.kjv: Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord’s house should be built.
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD of Heaven’s Armies says: These people say, 'The time has not yet come to rebuild the LORD’s temple.'

verses.kjv: Then came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet, saying,
verses.decoded: Then the LORD spoke again through the prophet Haggai, saying,

verses.kjv: Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?
verses.decoded: Is it right for you to live in your paneled houses while this house remains in ruins?

verses.kjv: Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways.
verses.decoded: Now this is what the LORD of Heaven’s Armies says: Think carefully about your actions.

verses.kjv: Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.
verses.decoded: You have planted a lot but harvested little. You eat, but never have enough. You drink, but never feel satisfied. You put on clothes, but never feel warm. And those who earn wages put them into a bag full of holes.

verses.kjv: Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways.
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD of Heaven’s Armies says: Think carefully about your actions.

verses.kjv: Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the Lord.
verses.decoded: Go up to the mountains, bring wood, and rebuild my temple. Then I will be pleased and honored, says the LORD.

verses.kjv: Ye looked for much, and, lo, it came to little; and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the Lord of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house.
verses.decoded: You expected a great harvest, but got little. When you brought it home, I blew it away. Why? Because my temple remains in ruins while each of you runs to your own house, says the LORD of Heaven’s Armies.

verses.kjv: Therefore the heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit.
verses.decoded: Because of this, the sky has stopped giving dew, and the earth has stopped producing crops.

verses.kjv: And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon the mountains, and upon the corn, and upon the new wine, and upon the oil, and upon that which the ground bringeth forth, and upon men, and upon cattle, and upon all the labour of the hands.
verses.decoded: I have sent a drought on the land, the mountains, the grain, the new wine, the olive oil, everything the ground produces, as well as on people and animals, and all the work of your hands.

verses.kjv: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him, and the people did fear before the Lord.
verses.decoded: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Josedech the high priest, and the rest of the people obeyed the LORD their God and the message from Haggai the prophet, as the LORD had sent him. The people were filled with reverent fear of the LORD.

verses.kjv: Then spake Haggai the Lord’s messenger in the Lord’s message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the Lord.
verses.decoded: Then Haggai, the LORD’s messenger, gave the LORD’s message to the people: 'I am with you,' says the LORD.

verses.kjv: And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God,
verses.decoded: Then the LORD encouraged the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, the spirit of Joshua son of Josedech, the high priest, and the spirit of the rest of the people. They came and began working on the LORD’s temple, the God of Heaven’s Armies.

verses.kjv: In the four and twentieth day of the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king.
verses.decoded: This happened on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.

verses.kjv: In the seventh month, in the one and twentieth day of the month, came the word of the Lord by the prophet Haggai, saying,
verses.decoded: On the 21st day of the seventh month, the LORD spoke through the prophet Haggai, saying,

verses.kjv: Speak now to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, and to the residue of the people, saying,
verses.decoded: Give this message to Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah; to Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and to the rest of the people:

verses.kjv: Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?
verses.decoded: Is there anyone left who saw the temple in its former glory? How do you see it now? Doesn’t it seem like nothing compared to before?

verses.kjv: Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the Lord; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord, and work: for I am with you, saith the Lord of hosts:
verses.decoded: But now, be strong, Zerubbabel, says the LORD; be strong, Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all you people of the land. Work hard, because I am with you, says the LORD of Heaven’s Armies.

verses.kjv: According to the word that I covenanted with you when ye came out of Egypt, so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not.
verses.decoded: Just as I promised when you came out of Egypt, my Spirit remains among you. Don’t be afraid.

verses.kjv: For thus saith the Lord of hosts; Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land;
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD of Heaven’s Armies says: In a little while, I will shake the heavens, the earth, the sea, and the dry land.

verses.kjv: And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.decoded: I will shake all nations, and the treasures of all nations will come here. I will fill this temple with glory, says the LORD of Heaven’s Armies.

verses.kjv: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.decoded: Silver and gold belong to me, says the LORD of Heaven’s Armies.

verses.kjv: The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the Lord of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.decoded: The glory of this new temple will be greater than the former one, says the LORD of Heaven’s Armies. And in this place, I will give peace, says the LORD of Heaven’s Armies.

verses.kjv: In the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet, saying,
verses.decoded: On the 24th day of the ninth month, in the second year of King Darius, the LORD spoke again through the prophet Haggai, saying,

verses.kjv: Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Ask now the priests concerning the law, saying,
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD of Heaven’s Armies says: Ask the priests about the law:

verses.kjv: If one bear holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his skirt do touch bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any meat, shall it be holy? And the priests answered and said, No.
verses.decoded: If someone carries holy meat in the edge of their garment and touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any food, will that food become holy? The priests answered, No.

verses.kjv: Then said Haggai, If one that is unclean by a dead body touch any of these, shall it be unclean? And the priests answered and said, It shall be unclean.
verses.decoded: Then Haggai asked, If someone who is ceremonially unclean because of touching a dead body touches any of these things, will they become unclean? The priests answered, Yes, they will become unclean.

verses.kjv: Then answered Haggai, and said, So is this people, and so is this nation before me, saith the Lord; and so is every work of their hands; and that which they offer there is unclean.
verses.decoded: Then Haggai said, This is how this people and nation are before me, says the LORD; everything they do and offer is unclean.

verses.kjv: And now, I pray you, consider from this day and upward, from before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the Lord:
verses.decoded: Now think carefully from this day forward—before any stone was laid on another in the LORD’s temple—

verses.kjv: Since those days were, when one came to an heap of twenty measures, there were but ten: when one came to the pressfat for to draw out fifty vessels out of the press, there were but twenty.
verses.decoded: Since those days, when someone expected to gather twenty measures, there were only ten; when someone went to press fifty vessels of oil, there were only twenty.

verses.kjv: I smote you with blasting and with mildew and with hail in all the labours of your hands; yet ye turned not to me, saith the Lord.
verses.decoded: I struck you with blight, mildew, and hail in all the work of your hands, but you did not turn back to me, says the LORD.

verses.kjv: Consider now from this day and upward, from the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, even from the day that the foundation of the Lord’s temple was laid, consider it.
verses.decoded: Think carefully from this day forward—from the 24th day of the ninth month, the day the LORD’s temple foundation was laid—reflect on this.

verses.kjv: Is the seed yet in the barn? yea, as yet the vine, and the fig tree, and the pomegranate, and the olive tree, hath not brought forth: from this day will I bless you.
verses.decoded: Is the seed still in the barn? No, the vine, fig tree, pomegranate, and olive tree have not yet produced fruit. But from this day on, I will bless you.

verses.kjv: And again the word of the Lord came unto Haggai in the four and twentieth day of the month, saying,
verses.decoded: Then the LORD’s message came to Haggai again on the 24th day of the month, saying,

verses.kjv: Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying, I will shake the heavens and the earth;
verses.decoded: Tell Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, ‘I will shake the heavens and the earth.’

verses.kjv: And I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms, and I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the heathen; and I will overthrow the chariots, and those that ride in them; and the horses and their riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother.
verses.decoded: I will bring down the thrones of kingdoms and destroy the power of foreign nations; I will overturn their chariots and riders, and they will fall, each by the sword of his own brother.

verses.kjv: In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the Lord, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.decoded: On that day, says the LORD of hosts, I will take you, Zerubbabel my servant, son of Shealtiel, and make you like a signet ring, because I have chosen you, says the LORD of hosts.
